items.english: Outside the door, darkened by now, there was the sound of hard wind and rain — a {t:arashi}.

The parents had gathered around the {t:table} under the dim {t:dento} hanging by the wall of the narrow room, about to take their supper. Father and mother were both still truly young. And the child was a girl, plump and round, just able to stand holding on to the {t:table}.
notes: p2-s3 fixes the child as a girl; Bōya later is kept as the parents' fond address, not a change of sex.

items.english: Neither the man nor the woman had yet a single wrinkle in the face. But in the hollowed, gentle-looking eyes in the shadow of the man's thick brows there showed a languid colour of tiredness. And in the dark colour of the woman's hair and about her slight shoulders there showed a still more sunken deep tiredness, and a drowsy-like peace.
notes: Keeps peace steady for the yasuraka- family; keeps young-and-already-worn together without ennobling.

items.english: The day had ended. The sadness and suffering of that day were about to flow into the peace of the night. And silent, smiling, they poured their eyes upon all that was the child.
notes: Keeps silent/smile/peace invariant; pours eyes rather than psychologising the gaze.

items.english: The child, standing precariously, with fat, round, ball-like short hands, was about to sweep at the things on the {t:table}, without leaving a moment's gap, and far too fast. So, smiling, they put everything — bowls and {t:dobin} and {t:alumi-nabe} and the rest — under the {t:table}. On top of the {t:table} there was left only the small spoon the child held and a single small plate.
notes: Clears the supper things under the table out of reach, as written; leaves spoon and plate as the only things above.

items.english: But the child, letting out a noisy shout full of small joy, banged spoon and plate down upon the {t:table}.

data.say: Drafted p1-p6 in past durative voice, keeping storm frame bare, supper business exact, and peace/silent/smile steady for the network.
